GPOs.Name: SEC-Require-SMBSigning-Server
GPOs.Description: Require SMB signing on servers for all connections to prevent SMB relay attacks
GPOs.NoteSummary: Server-side signing alone is what stops SMB relay
GPOs.Note:
Requiring SMB signing on the server side is what actually defeats SMB relay, which is why LOCKmeAD ships no client-side counterpart.

In a relay attack the attacker coerces a victim into authenticating to a host under their control, then replays that authentication against one of your machines. The attacker never holds the session key, so the relayed session cannot be signed. A server that requires signing rejects it outright.

Enforcing 'require signing' on the client side only protects a client that connects to a malicious server. It does nothing to stop your own machines from being relayed to, which is the path that matters here.

Keep in mind that every Windows host acts as an SMB server, not just file servers: the LanmanServer service runs on workstations too, and workstations are common relay targets. Link this GPO broadly rather than to server OUs only.

SecurityOptions.Description: Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees)
Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)

GPOs.Name: SEC-Kerberos-EnforceAES-DCs
GPOs.Description: Disables RC4 at the domain level on domain controllers by setting DefaultDomainSupportedEncTypes to 0x38 (AES128, AES256, Future). This prevents the KDC from issuing RC4 tickets even when an account's msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes is blank. WARNING: May be too aggressive for most organizations - only apply after all service accounts have been remediated and no RC4-dependent devices remain.

RegistryPreferences.Description: KDC default encryption types - AES128 (0x8) + AES256 (0x10) + Future (0x20) = 0x38. Disables RC4 and DES fallback for accounts with no msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes set.

GPOs.Name: SEC-Kerberos-EnforceAES-Clients
GPOs.Description: Restrict Kerberos encryption to AES128, AES256, and Future types only - disables RC4 and DES on clients. WARNING: Only apply to devices confirmed to have no RC4 dependencies (verify via Event ID 4768 Advertised Etypes). Devices with RC4-only keytabs, legacy NAS, or non-Windows appliances will break if targeted before remediation.

SecurityOptions.Description: Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos - AES128_HMAC_SHA1 (0x8) + AES256_HMAC_SHA1 (0x10) + Future (0x7FFFFFE0) = 0x7FFFFFF8. Disables DES and RC4.
